scheduling.reason: Candidate records are proposals only; this audit does not change roadmap, business scope, or orchestration policy.

candidates.title: Align the new-customer form with persisted customer data
candidates.problem: The UI accepts customer identity, second contact, address, and tag inputs that the current create payload/schema/model discard.
acceptance: Every retained form field is included in validated create/update DTOs and persists tenant-scoped.
A reload reproduces each retained submitted value.
Create/update remain tenant-isolated and write auditable mutations.
Any field deliberately out of scope is removed or disabled before data entry rather than silently discarded.

candidates.title: Make customer post-save shortcuts execute or remove them
candidates.problem: Visit and address shortcuts change local state but have no submit-time effect.
acceptance: Selecting a supported shortcut produces its stated result after customer save.
Failed downstream creation leaves an actionable error and does not misreport success.
Unsupported shortcuts are absent or disabled with an explanation before selection.
Any created appointment/address is tenant-scoped and auditable.

candidates.title: Honor customer preselection in quote creation
candidates.problem: Customer-detail and post-create CTAs provide client_id, but the quote editor ignores it.
acceptance: A valid client_id from a customer-origin quote CTA preselects that customer after list load.
An invalid, inaccessible, or absent client_id leaves selection safe and displays no forged state.
The final quote retains backend tenant ownership validation.

candidates.title: Remove silent loss of quote internal notes
candidates.problem: Quote internal notes are accepted in the editor but omitted from the request and domain schema.
acceptance: The editor either persists internal notes in a private quote field or removes the field from the shipped form.
Persisted notes round-trip on edit/detail and never render in public approval/PDF output.
The mutation remains tenant-scoped and auditable.

candidates.title: Replace customer-profile mock tabs with customer-scoped data
candidates.problem: The profile passes an empty quote list, hard-codes identity pills, and renders generic empty content for other entity tabs.
acceptance: Quotes, work orders, appointments, payments, and audit history shown on a profile are filtered by customer and current tenant.
A profile never exposes another customer or tenant's records.
Each tab distinguishes loaded-empty, loading, and request-error states.
Identity labels derive from persisted data rather than literals.

candidates.title: Make company identity controls persist brand color and logo
candidates.problem: Identity visual controls are rendered active but have no handler; persistence fields exist but are absent from the profile contract.
acceptance: Logo replacement has validation, loading/error feedback, tenant-bound storage, persistence, and audit evidence.
Color selection is keyboard-accessible, saves, reloads, and records an audited company mutation.
Identity values are used only after backend authorization and plan rules allow them.

candidates.title: Implement the new-customer Save and new action
candidates.problem: Save and new is a disabled dead CTA beside the working save action.
acceptance: Save and new submits the same validated customer creation request once.
On success it clears form state for a new customer and confirms success without duplication.
On failure it preserves entered data and exposes existing error treatment.

candidates.title: Make fixed-grid web forms usable at narrow viewports
candidates.problem: Several page-local inline grids bypass the shared responsive grid rules; the new-customer address grid alone has 542px of fixed columns before gaps, so fields can overflow their narrower parent.
acceptance: The audited create/detail/settings/dashboard/plan layouts reflow or provide an intentional accessible scroll treatment at narrow widths without clipping a field or primary CTA.
The customer address form preserves its field order, labels, validation, and submission payload through the reflow.
Desktop layouts retain their existing information hierarchy and controls.
Browser coverage verifies a narrow viewport and a desktop viewport for each affected layout family.
